hypothesis: A bigger prefill chunk leaves each worker more compute per request to hide behind the next block's reads, so read-ahead gains more at GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK=256 than at 128, still without changing any token.
model: GLM-5.3-Flash (a community abliterated fine-tune; same architecture and tensor shapes), Colibri int4-gs64 streaming container, 195.8 GB
command: make -C c glm53 (coordinator and workers); workers: EXPERT_WORKER=1 CLUSTER_WORKER_PORT=9100 GLM53_EXPERT_GB=<10|6.7> OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 ./glm53 (SNAP=<model>); coordinator: GLM53_PREFILL_CHUNK=256 OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 COLI_CLUSTER_WEIGHTS=52,48 CLUSTER_WORKERS=<worker-a>:9100,<worker-b>:9100 GLM53_VERBOSE=2 ./glm53 --model <model> --prompt "$(cat prompt.txt)" --greedy 1; tok_s = 245 / (prefill seconds printed on stderr); arms alternated B,C after one warmup

hardware.ram: coordinator 31 GB DDR4; workers 15 GB each
